newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries climb in London, ignore plunging dollar.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries climb in London, ignore plunging dollar.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries managed to inch ahead in London trade on Wednesday despite a shaky dollar, and dealers said the market appeared well-underpinned at present levels.
"I'm a bit surprised we're as strong as we are given what's been happening to the dollar," said one trader.
The dollar slumped to a seven-month low against the yen on Wednesday amid fears of rising trade tensions.

But Treasuries held up well, with the 30-year cash bond at 97-15 to yield 6.82 percent by 1015 GMT, up from 97-12 in Tokyo and 97-08 at the New York close. The 10-year was at 100-18, up from 100-16 in Tokyo and 100-13 in New York.

One trader noted good U.S. hedge fund buying in Treasuries, particularly in the 10-year sector. He said the outlook for the market was fairly positive, despite the risk of a major correction in the dollar.
"I'm not convinced the market will suffer a major setback, even if the currency does start to get hit," he said.
Michael Derks, cross market fixed income strategist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, agreed. "I shouldn't imagine they'll be an enormous impact from the dollar," he said.
Derks said if anything, he expected the market to rally from here and yields to fall a bit further.

A dearth of data on Wednesday left investors looking to Thursday's May retail sales data. Derks said the market had largely discounted the May data, but added a significant upward revision to April figures could cause an upset.
According to a Reuter survey, economists expected retail sales to rise 0.4 percent in May after a 0.3 percent fall in April.
By 1032 GMT, September T-bonds were up 5/32 at 110-22. One trader said he expected the contract to test 111-00 and noted sentiment was still quite positive.
